evidence: Cic. N. D. 2.122: alia sūgunt, alia carpunt, alia vorant, alia mandunt
Plin. NH 17.54: asinī lentissimē mandunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The classical verb for chewing (Cicero, Pliny). Not mandō, mandāre, entrust.
The lengthened, everyday form of mandō: ante-classical and post-Augustan (Lewis & Short). Augustus has it in a letter (“I ate two mouthfuls”), and it became the Romance word for eating.

phrases.english: Chew your food well before you swallow it.

phrases.latin: alia sūgunt, alia carpunt, alia vorant, alia mandunt
phrases.english: some suck, some graze, some gulp their food down, some chew it

sources: Lewis & Short: manduco · Lewis & Short: lentus · Lewis & Short: mando
